I created `packages/core/src/handle.ts` with exactly the exports the spec lists, in the same style as `src/index.ts`. Every function body is `throw new Error("not implemented");`. Both constants are real exports with their values (3 and 30), not declarations. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors and the existing suite still passes (13 of 13). I deleted the `dist-test` build output afterwards, since it wasn't there when I started.

Three things to know:
- **No `throws` notes in the doc comments.** The spec says no export throws for any string input, so no function documents one.
- **No new error classes.** Bad input comes back as an `invalid` result, as the spec describes.
- **`index.ts` is unchanged.** The spec says `packages/core/src/index.ts` gains `export * from "./handle.js";`, but you asked for the seam file only. That line is left for the implementer to add. Until they do, the scenario that imports the handle names from the package entry will fail.

Added: HANDLE_MIN_LENGTH, HANDLE_MAX_LENGTH, HandleProblem, HandleRejected, HandleCheck, toHandleCase, checkHandle, NormalizedHandle, normalizeHandle, isValidHandle, toHandleStem, handleStemFromEmail

public.finalText:
I wrote the test suite in `packages/core/test/handles-check.test.ts`. It covers all 33 scenarios in the spec (10 `@happy`, 15 `@boundary`, 8 `@unhappy`), with two tests each. The first test checks the scenario's own example table. The second checks an edge case that follows directly from the same rule, for example:

- characters just outside the allowed ranges (`` ` ``, `{`, `/`, `:`)
- an emoji that pushes a handle to 31 code units
- hyphens being trimmed before the cut to 30, not after
- a Kelvin-sign-only handle
- lone surrogates that must not cause a throw

`npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors. Running the tests gives 2 passes and 64 failures, as expected while the function bodies still throw. The 2 that pass check the two length constants, which are already set in `handle.ts`.

Choices the implementer should know about:

- **Package entry tests:** the `[happy-10]` tests import `../src/index.js` as a namespace and look the handle names up at runtime. That keeps the file compiling before `index.ts` gets its `export * from "./handle.js"` line. Those tests fail until that line is added.
- **"No other exports":** this rule isn't in any scenario, so I keyed it to `[happy-10]`. It checks that `handle.ts` exports exactly the eight runtime names.
- **Special characters:** the spec's non-ASCII values (no-break space, Kelvin sign, dotted capital I, emoji) are written as `\u` escapes in the tests, taken from the actual characters in `spec.md`.

I changed nothing outside the test file.

66 tests, in 1 file.
